description: One tested build. Send it in parts while you test: each lite record call with --draft saves its parts. The last call without --draft adds its parts, or {}, and Checkmate checks the full record. A part replaces an earlier part with the same ID, or a check with the same item and check. Leave out each optional field that you do not need. When Checkmate refuses, read each reason and hint. A refused call saves nothing and the drafts stay, so send again only the refused parts, with the fixes. Only the PM answers questions and accepts records.

items.description: New rules that you found and that no item covers, with the source exploration or docs/<file>#<section>.

checks.description: One or more checks for each item. For each rule, also try the boundary value, the other entry point (API or UI), the state after an undo or a removal, and a second view of the same value (a list, an export, a header).

defects.description: The new defects of this build, each with exact steps, the expected result and its source (the ticket, a doc, or a PM answer), and evidence. A failed check names each defect. When no item covers it, add an item. Give an earlier defect a verdict in retests.

retests.description: A verdict for each open earlier defect: do its steps again before you explore, then give fixed or not_fixed, what you saw, and evidence from this build. For not_fixed, also add a failed check that names the defect ID.

questions.description: New open points for the PM. Do not ask a question again.

changes.description: Changed areas that you found after the checklist, in the form of the checklist field changes.

evidence.description: Each entry is a file path in the workspace (a screenshot, a response, a log), for example evidence/r1.png, or a short text of what you saw, for example GET /api/loans/L1: 200 fee 1.50. One file can be the evidence of several checks.

id.description: A new unique item ID, for example R9.

source.description: Where the rule comes from: exploration, or docs/<file>#<section>.

check.description: What you did, in one sentence. Leave it out on a check of a repeat line: Checkmate uses the steps of the line.

result.description: passed, failed, blocked (the check cannot run), or not_run (you did not run it). A criterion item needs passed, failed, or blocked. Leave it out with value on an item with a repeat line.

observed.description: What you saw. Necessary for passed and failed without value.

value.description: Necessary for each repeat line: do its steps again and give the value that you see. Checkmate compares it with the reference value after it removes the spaces at the two ends, changes each sequence of spaces to one space, and writes each number in one form (1.50 is 1.5, 007 is 7). All other text must be equal. Equal: passed. Different: the check needs defect (failed), intended (passed), or a result and a reason when the difference is not in the rule, for example a generated ID or data that your tests changed. On an item without a reference value, a passed check with value sets the reference value.

reason.description: Necessary for blocked and not_run: why the check did not run. With a value that is different from the reference value and no defect or intended: why the difference is not in the rule.

intended.description: Only for a different value that is correct because the ticket or a PM answer changes the rule. Then the check is passed and the value becomes the reference value.

note.description: Why the new value is correct.

source.description: The ticket line, PM answer, or doc that changes the rule, for example Q1.

defect.description: Necessary on a failed check, and only there: a new defect ID from defects, or an open defect with the verdict not_fixed.

id.description: A new defect ID, for example D1.

severity.description: low, medium, high, or critical: the effect on the user.

expected.description: The correct result and its source.

evidence.description: One or more entries in the form of checks[].evidence.

defect.description: The ID of the open earlier defect.

verdict.description: fixed or not_fixed. For not_fixed, also add a failed check that names this ID in defect.

observed.description: What you saw when you did the steps of the defect again.

evidence.description: One or more entries that show the result on this build.

id.description: A new question ID, for example Q1.

question.description: One clear question for the PM.

items.description: The IDs of the items that the answer changes.
